_note: Role defaults used by `dcsim prepare` to size the baseline production plan from simulated demand at typical (neutral) popularity. station_dilution: each item's popularity is divided by (same-role items at its station)^dilution, so a station with 5 sushi rolls doesn't get 5x the demand of a one-entree station. PLACEHOLDERS until staff estimates. planner.reorder_factor raised 0.8 -> 1.2 on 2026-11-12 so the 3,000-student crowd rarely runs out (team: food rarely runs out late on a normal day). planner_by_period.late_night (2026-11-13, engine 0.4.2): late-night demand collapses after ~10:30 pm, so once fewer than 1.5 batches are still to be eaten the kitchen cooks top-up batches of 25% with a matching reorder point, and keeps no spare batches. Cut late-night waste from ~41% to ~20% of cooked portions with about the same stockout minutes. Tuning choice, not staff-confirmed.

resources._note: Kitchen capacity (IMPROVEMENTS 1.3, engine 0.5.0). PLACEHOLDER GUESSES (2026-11-13), not staff numbers: cooks per service period, equipment units (each holds one batch), hands-on prep minutes per batch (inside cook_min), and which equipment each dish uses. Sized so the baseline plan rarely waits; very small or very frequent batches queue for cooks and equipment. Chosen 2026-11-13 from unconstrained peak use (ovens 14-16, steamers 7-8, flat-tops 5-6) and a cook sweep on Nov 13: 12 dinner / 4 late-night cooks are busy ~63% and barely move the baseline (waste -2%); 8/3 cooks make stockouts ~6x worse.
